title: The Birth of Ishmael and the Significance of the Text
english: It becomes divine: 'For your lightnings have appeared to the inhabited world' (Ps 103:4). Gen 16:15–16. And Hagar bore a son to Abram, and Abram called the name of his son whom Hagar bore, Ishmael. And Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.

It may be said that for the sake of solemnity and authenticity, the phrase 'Hagar bore a son to Abram' lies [there] with observation, but the following is clear regarding the spoken word; let us also consider these matters. The one making progress, when he brings forth toward the goal of the teacher, that which is being brought forth is not easy to misinterpret. Therefore, the appropriate word of the birth applies to the one rightly educating and sowing what is profitable; it said, 'Hagar bore a son to Abram' (Gen 16:15). Since this is so... providing what the Scripture says, it is brought forward: 'And Abram called the name of his son' (Gen 16:11), and it leads to 'whom she bore to him' (Gen 16:15); for if not for the meaning which he had, the phrase 'And Abram called the name of his son' would have sufficed, without adding 'whom she bore to him.'

And these things are enough for now; let us see also that concerning the numbers of the years of the patriarch; for it is said: 'Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram' (Gen 16:16). Both the numbers are... [Gaps]... Gen 17:1. And Abram was ninety-nine years old, and the Lord appeared to him.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Call of Abraham and the Nature of God
english: To Abram it was said: 'I am your God; be pleasing before me and become blameless' (Gen 17:1). The number hundred is composed of ten tens; and these [those] rolling [moving] were said to be squares, and the square shape is stable. [Gaps] ... again then God appeared to Abraham, a lover of mankind, in order to appear and qualify him to be God, saying, 'I am your God' (Gen 17:1). And he is not the God of the saints [gaps] but being the Creator of all, indeed of heaven and earth and those in them, becoming God absolutely according to their worship [gaps] ... it is said: 'The God, my God,' declaring by the word that the God of all things and of me, and as one serving you, you are God. And he leads him into a struggle and a preparation of manliness, the [saying] 'Be pleasing before me' [gaps] ...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Covenant and the Multiplication of Nations
english: And I will multiply your covenant through me and through you exceedingly. Let there be no blame found against me. He promised to multiply himself according to the word, and this is no wonder. For other nations have also become many. And Abraham fell upon his face. They are rejoicing and being multiplied just as the patriarch. And God spoke to him, saying: 'And behold, my covenant is with you, and you shall be a father of a multitude of nations. And your name shall not be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham, because a father of many nations I have made you. And I will multiply you exceedingly, exceedingly.' Again, the Lord, after the falling, confirms the promise, saying to him that He will make a covenant with him; and he shall be a father of a multitude.
